note: What is machine-enforced versus what is convention.

enforced.assetRolePinnedPolicies: verify_all.py and semantic_validate.py check the EXACT value for 5 compliance-critical roles, not just enum membership
enforced.motionFieldClosure: schema (additionalProperties false on the motion object)
enforced.copyBudgets: maxLength in the schema; maxWords in semantic_validate.py
enforced.manifestCounts: extraction/verify_all.py (recomputed from disk, not read back)

conventionOnly.spacing: There is NO uniform spacing scale on this site. Every section carries its own measured padding. tokens/00-foundation/spacing.json records the real inventory, and nothing machine-checks a generated instance against it, because a PageSpec carries no spacing field.
conventionOnly.semanticRoleUsage: A PageSpec has no per-instance style or token-override field at all — styling is fully owned by the section and component contracts. So there is no PageSpec-level token reference for a validator to check. This is recorded plainly rather than inventing a field in order to have something to validate.
conventionOnly.responsiveBehaviour: Each section contract carries a structured `responsive` block cited against real CSS, but a PageSpec cannot override it.

rawValueRestrictions.note: Category keys here match the real catalog keys in token-catalog.json, not convenient human labels.
rawValueRestrictions.color: forbidden — reference a palette or semanticRole id
rawValueRestrictions.radius: restricted — only the closed brandRadius domain is settable per instance
rawValueRestrictions.easing: restricted — only the 3 closed easing ids
rawValueRestrictions.breakpoint: forbidden — responsive behaviour is contract-owned, not instance-owned
